panel.foldHint: Fold it into the lower right corner to see what it covers; click the round button to open it again

sourceHint.project: The project’s own; this is what you edit
sourceHint.base: From the game or the base mod; taken into the project on the first save
sourceHint.modFile: In the mod’s files: kept as it was at import, or copied in from the base game to change

panel.notInProjectHistory: This country’s start comes from the game itself and the project has no history file for it, so it can’t be edited here. It isn’t copied into the project automatically: the game would then run the same start twice, doubling political power and equipment designs.
panel.move: Drag to move the panel · double-click to put it back on the right

baseText.originVanilla: This is base-game content and is not in your project data.
baseText.originVanillaIn: This is base-game content ({file}) and is not in your project data.
baseText.originMod: This is in the mod’s original files and was not split into project data.
baseText.originModIn: This is in the mod’s original files ({file}) and was not split into project data.
baseText.originUnknown: This is not in the project data (it comes from the base game or a mod file).
baseText.heading: Edit text
baseText.note: This changes the text the game shows in the current language; it goes into the mod’s replace localisation and into the exported mod as well.
baseText.noteShared: This base-game text is shared by every country; changing it changes it for all of them.
baseText.logicNote: Costs, conditions and the like cannot be changed here yet.
baseText.logicNoteDecision: Cost, icon and days are changed below, under “Copy into my mod to edit”.
baseText.emptyPlaceholder: The base game has no text here; whatever you write will be shown

politics.startUnhired: {name} is no longer hired at the start

person.name: Name
person.createNote: Saved as a project person (the same one the characters workbench shows) and written into {tag}’s starting history on export, so they are there from the start. After creating, change the portrait in the panel on the right (upload, asset library, AI generation); add skills in the workbench.
person.switcherHint: Pick someone to edit, or create one

problem.nameInvalid: The name cannot contain quotes or line breaks
problem.slotRequired: Choose a seat for the advisor
problem.ideologyRequired: Choose an ideology for the country leader

spirit.manageStart: Which national spirits it starts with…
spirit.created: Created national spirit {name}; {tag} starts with it
spirit.createAndAdd: Create and add to the start
spirit.createNote: The new entry is saved in the national spirits workbench; once created, the same national spirit editor opens to keep editing.

country.takeInHint: This country is not in the project yet. Editing it adds it to the project exactly as the game has it, changing nothing; it then shows up in the workbench too.
country.takeInFailed: Could not add it to the project. Please try again.

page.designSavedStartedOob: Saved to the mod: “{name}” (this country had no order of battle file; created {file}, which the export writes into history/units and loads in the country’s history)
page.designSavedImported: Saved to the mod: “{name}” (first save: the whole {file} file was taken into the project)
page.doctrineNotInHistory: This country’s starting doctrine is not in its history script (it comes from elsewhere), so it cannot be changed here
page.focusTreeNotInProject: This focus tree is not in the project data (it comes from the base game or a mod file); import it into the project to edit it here.
page.focusMissing: This tree in the project has no {id}.
page.focusMissingThis: This tree in the project does not have this focus.
page.continuousKind: Focus tree · {id} · continuous focus panel position
page.mapModeNotBuilt: The “{mode}” map mode is not built yet; for now the map has only army strategy (political), naval and air strategy (strategic regions)
page.buttonNotBuilt: This button does nothing in the editor yet
page.mapNamesUpdate: Names and colours on the map update in a few seconds
page.pickFocusPrompt: Click a focus in the tree to make it {what} of “{name}”

uiEdit.flagNote: This draws the country’s flag (the game picks it by country and ideology); to change it, change the country’s own flag pictures.
uiEdit.editCountryFlag: Change the flag in the country profile
uiEdit.glossSummary: Replace the gloss over the flag (advanced)
uiEdit.textNote: This changes the localisation key itself: every place that uses it changes, in the exported mod too.

scope.allCountries: Every country shares this text: changing it changes it for all of them, in the exported mod too.
scope.country: This changes the text for this country only; other countries keep theirs. The exported mod gets it too.

uiEdit.guiNote: These words were written straight into the interface file. Saving gives them a localisation key of their own and puts the words in the mod’s localisation; the interface file is exported with the mod.
uiEdit.personNote: This changes the person’s name: everywhere the game shows this person, in the exported mod too.
uiEdit.notExportable: This interface file is neither the base game’s nor the imported mod’s own, so the export cannot carry a change to it; its words cannot be changed here yet.
uiEdit.ownedByProject: The project’s own data writes this text ({file}); the export keeps the data’s text, so a change here would not show. Change it in that data’s own editor (the person, the country profile…).
uiEdit.nothing: This element has no picture to replace or text to change.

reason.runtimeCountry: The game writes this from the country’s data while running; it changes when the country’s data changes
reason.literal: This text is written into an interface file the export cannot carry; it cannot be changed here yet
reason.runtime: The game generates this text while running; it cannot be changed yet
reason.computed: The game works this number out while running; there is no text behind it to change
reason.placeholder: The interface file only holds a stand-in here; the game replaces it while running, so a change would never show

uiEdit.removeHint: Takes it off this screen. An element of the base game or the mod is hidden: it is not seen in the game, but the game's code still finds it, so it cannot crash the game, and it can be shown again at any time. An element you added yourself is deleted.
uiEdit.hiddenNote: Hidden: not seen in the game or in the game view, only faintly in UI editing so it can be shown again.
uiEdit.removeNotExportable: Changes to this screen's file cannot go into the export, so it cannot be deleted here yet.

sprite.frames: {frames} frames, this is frame {frame}; a new picture replaces the whole strip
sprite.hint: After choosing a picture, drag the box over the part to use; it is scaled to the slot's size. If it may look distorted you are told, and can convert it to a suitable size in one click. A picture for several frames uses this part in every frame.
sprite.restored: Original picture restored; its file was removed from the mod as well
sprite.exportGfx: Written into the mod and packed on export: new picture {texture}; {gfx} is copied whole into the project, with only this sprite pointing at the new picture
sprite.exportPath: Written into the mod and packed on export: new picture {texture}, at the same path as the game’s original, so the game reads it
sprite.exportNone: Replaced in the game view only; the exported mod will not have this picture
sprite.exportNoneWhy: Replaced in the game view only; the exported mod will not have this picture ({error})
sprite.ownHint: Only the selected element changes: it gets a picture of its own, and everything else using the original keeps it.
sprite.ownDone: New picture in place, used by this element only
sprite.exportOwn: Written into the mod and packed on export: new picture {texture}, used by this element only; everything else keeps the original

changeLog.heading: Changes since this page opened
changeLog.empty: No changes yet. What you save in an edit panel is listed here and can be undone.

error.gone: This item is no longer in the project, so it cannot be undone
error.changedSince: This item changed again after this save (in the workbench, for example); undoing would lose those changes, so it was not undone
error.notAllBack: The undo did not put everything back; these still have the changed values: {fields}

components.title: Components
components.dragHint: Drag onto the screen · double-click words to edit · Delete removes
components.unmountable: Components go on the politics, decisions, research, diplomacy, trade, construction, production, deployment, logistics or focus screen
components.placeFailed: Could not put it on the screen
components.loadFailed: This component could not be read
components.exportNote: Exported, it is mounted on this screen in the game ({mount}), where you see it here
components.deleteBody: It is taken off this screen.

hint.window_panel: A window in the base game's style: a title and a close button, on no screen, opened by a button
hint.box: The game's bordered window; holds other components and stretches
hint.scroll_box: A bordered container; components past its height scroll with a scrollbar and the mouse wheel
hint.list: Rows made from an array (with a scrollbar): one row per element; what you put in is one row
hint.grid: A grid made from an array, four cells a row, a picture in each
hint.group: A container that isn't drawn: groups components so they move together
hint.title: The title font (the small capitals the game's screen titles use)
hint.paragraph: Text that wraps at the box's width; stretch it wider or taller
hint.button: The game's standard button (261×34); its picture keeps its own size
hint.wide_button: The game's stretchable button: any width or height without distortion
hint.image_button: A picture used as a button, without words
hint.switch: A checkbox-style switch: a click turns it on or off, kept in a variable
hint.icon: A picture (a focus question-mark icon to start with)
hint.divider: The divider line the game's screens use
hint.progressbar: A bar whose frame follows a variable

components.defaultParagraph: Several lines of text: the game wraps them at the box's width.
components.undoFailed: Couldn't undo — refresh and try again
components.unmountableWindowOk: This screen can't hold components: put down a window panel, or drop into one already here
components.openersNone: No button opens it yet: in the game it can't be opened
components.addOpener: Put an open button on this screen
components.addOpenerUnmountable: Open a screen that holds components (politics, decisions …) first
components.openerPlaced: Open button placed; a second click closes the panel
components.windowMoveable: The player can drag this window
components.deletePanelBody: The panel and its components are deleted; you can undo it.
components.exportNoteWindow: Exported, it is a window of its own on the game's main screen, where you see it here
components.windowGrip: Drag to move the window; click to edit the panel
components.paletteGrip: Drag to move the component bar · double-click to put it back at the right edge

layout.unnamed: This element has no name in its interface file, so it can't be moved; you can still change its picture and words
layout.notExportable: This interface file can't be written into the mod, so the position was not saved
layout.failed: The position was not saved; please try again

countryTakenIn: {name} is now in the project; you’ll find it in the workbench.
